raw_response:
I am already old, and with only two people in the house, I cannot spread myself too thin. Some of the family works off-farm, so I have to keep the field plan steady and manageable. I will still do what I know best: keep most of the land in wheat-maize, because that gives me grain and more stable cash flow, and leave a smaller part in cotton, because cotton can still bring money if the price is decent. I do not want to gamble too much this year. Fertilizer is expensive, irrigation from the well costs money, and at my age I do not want a plan that looks good on paper but I cannot finish in time.

For wheat, I will follow the usual local timing. I usually put base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once at jointing if the stand looks good. The extension guy said not to push N too high, but if the wheat looks pale I still add a bit, because under-fertilizing hurts yield more than wasting a little fertilizer. After wheat harvest, I have to turn around fast for maize, so I will keep the maize area on the same wheat fields and use simple rotary tillage or direct seeding if I can hire the machine in time. For cotton, I will keep it on a smaller block. Cotton takes more watching and more hand work, so I cannot put too much area there now. I will irrigate when the crop stage really needs it, not too many times, because pumping water costs real money.
